edits.text: - Fallback ordering: when comparing two candidate cuts on the source surface, if one cut falls immediately after a determiner, pronoun, auxiliary or preposition and the next token is the syntactic head or a required complement of the ensuing noun/verb phrase, prefer the other cut (i.e. prefer keeping that function word with its following head/complement).

- Fallback ordering: when comparing two candidate cuts on the source surface, prefer a cut that falls outside a multi-word proper name or title or a short comma-separated list over a cut that lies between the words of that name/list; if a cut must be placed near such a name/list, prefer the cut immediately after the full name/list rather than inside it.

- Keep a function word (determiner, pronoun, auxiliary or preposition) together with the immediately following content word when that word is the head or required complement completing the noun or verb phrase.

- Keep contiguous runs of two or more capitalized content words (multiword names/titles) together; for short comma-separated lists of such names (≤3 items), prefer a cut after the entire list rather than between items.

- Fallback ordering: when comparing two candidate cuts on the source surface, prefer the cut that keeps a short function word (determiner/pronoun/auxiliary/preposition) adjacent to the immediately following head or required complement (noun, verb, numeral, or multiword name).

- Fallback ordering: when comparing two candidate cuts where one produces a one-token segment that is a function word (determiner, pronoun, auxiliary, or preposition) immediately before a content head or required complement, prefer the cut that keeps that function word adjacent to the following head/complement.

edits._was: - Is the cut inside noun-internal material (possessives, appositives, dense nominal modifiers) that would detach modifiers or heads and thereby change who or what is being described?
